neighbours.label: fiction: the first word of narration resuming right after a line of dialogue ('"...," she said. / We were quiet as ...')
fire:
"Don't wait up for me," he said.
I watched his car disappear down the road.

"We should go," Mara whispered.
We slipped out through the kitchen door.

"Is it over?" asked Tom.
I nodded and handed him the letter.

"Thank you for everything," she said.
We stood on the porch until the taxi came.

"You're late again," said the captain.
I mumbled an apology and took my seat.

"Keep your voice down," Ellen hissed.
We crouched behind the hedge and waited.

"Where were you last night?" my mother asked.
I stared at my shoes and said nothing.

"It's beautiful," Sam breathed.
We sat by the lake as the sun went down.

The report covered three years of data.
I checked the figures against the archive.

Our team finished the survey early.
We sent the results to the board.

The policy changed in March.
I updated the handbook to match it.

The workshop ran for two days.
We stood near the entrance to greet guests.

The budget was approved last week.
I submitted the forms to the office.

The clinic opened a new wing.
We toured the building with the director.

The library extended its hours.
I usually study there in the evenings.

The lake is popular with visitors.
We recommend arriving early in the day.
